name: mean_reversion_hull_ma
mechanism: On NIFTY, during mid-session ranging periods (flat HMA slope), the Hull Moving Average over 3 minutes (36 × 5s bars) serves as a real-time equilibrium anchor because its lag-less construction tracks where sustained institutional order flow has been placed. When NIFTY deviates >0.12% (≈25-27 spot points) from this HMA while the slope is near-zero, VWAP-benchmarked execution algos and market makers see the index as statistically cheap or expensive relative to recent flow — their delta-hedging and mean-reversion fills push price back toward the HMA within 30-90 seconds. The flat-slope filter is critical: it rules out trending regimes where the overshoot is justified by sustained directional order flow, isolating only the pure microstructure overshoots.
core_signal_oneliner: Price deviating more than 0.12% from a flat 3-minute Hull Moving Average, signaling a microstructure overshoot in a ranging regime
